article.name: DreamGraph
article.summary: DreamGraph is a project-scoped cognitive graph for software projects. It separates speculative hypotheses from validated project knowledge, evaluates normalization claims against source and human evidence, and retrieves bounded graph context. This is a source-based review; no system, tests, or benchmarks were run.

who_what.text: The official README describes DreamGraph as a graph-governed development environment for software projects, with daemon, MCP tools, CLI, VS Code extension, Explorer and browser Architect surfaces.
The official repository page identifies main as default; its main commit feed reports full head 41f65091746bc1cf0ac17e34eedda6d29973f9f0 updated 2026-10-09T06:30:46Z.

architecture.text: DreamGraph maintains a fact graph for project entities and validated relationships, alongside a separate dream graph for candidate hypotheses. The documented entities include features, workflows, data-model entities, ADRs, UI elements and tensions; instance graph state is stored in JSON files.

Dream candidates carry fields such as confidence, plausibility, evidence, contradiction, origin strategy, TTL, reinforcement count and lifecycle status. Candidate normalization outcomes, validated edges and tensions have distinct persistent stores.
The architecture describes UUID-scoped instances attached to projects, with repository bindings controlling which paths are in bounds.

behavior.text: Scans and enrichment populate project entities; dream strategies add speculative nodes and edges; normalization evaluates candidates and publishes accepted graph changes through the shared publication boundary.

The normalization evidence ledger models claim observations as supporting or contradicting and records origin, ancestry, operation identity, observation time and optional source proof. A source proof binds a configured repository and path to a content hash, JSON pointer and independence ID; the implementation checks scope, bytes and the selected JSON value.

Cognitive curation supports reject, retire, reopen, restore and assert actions bound to a graph revision, actor and reason; it stores disposition history and supports reversible hash-bound archives. The evidence ledger records withdrawals separately.

Canonical RAG uses a read-only context-pack path and reports included records, token count and selection details. The legacy path uses lexical TF-IDF matching and graph expansion but has fewer supported controls; canonical retrieval is the current default.

The inspected architecture documents per-instance project/repository boundaries. The evidence reader rejects absolute and parent-traversal paths and symlinks outside a configured repository. No cross-instance isolation testing was performed.

Claim-specific provenance distinguishes source-backed, human-asserted and derived claims; source observations can be withdrawn. This does not establish complete source provenance for every graph entity or mutation surface.

The normalizer yields to the event loop in batches. Graph publication records revisions, content hashes, receipts and journal state, while cognitive-store reads reject published-content mismatches instead of treating them as empty state. These are code observations, not measured results.

metrics.text: Answerable retrieval accuracy and abstention — unmeasured. No answerable or abstention cases were scored.
Correction accuracy and stale-value rate — unmeasured. No post-correction recall probes were run.
Deletion leakage — unmeasured. No post-removal probes or backup/snapshot checks were run.
Scope isolation — unmeasured. No cross-instance, project, or repository probes were run.
Evidence support precision and citation coverage — unmeasured. No generated claims were adjudicated against stored evidence.
Retrieval latency and write-to-recall delay — unmeasured. No reads, writes or recall timings were collected.
Tokens and cost — unmeasured. No token counts or provider charges were collected.
Storage efficiency — unmeasured. No corpus or persistent-byte measurements were made.

limits.text: This is a selected source review of the README, architecture/cognitive/data-model guides, and current retrieval, normalization, evidence, curation, publication and store code. It did not inspect every graph write API, plugin/client, deployment or recovery/export route.

The inspected evidence gate applies to cognitive normalization. Provenance coverage across all entity types and mutation surfaces, practical isolation, backup retention, concurrency under load, and generated-claim quality remain unknown or unmeasured.
The pinned official README and SECURITY.md were checked for contact. Neither publishes a contact email; the record stores null and the exact checked URLs.

benchmark.note: No DreamGraph runtime, tests, or benchmark workload was executed. Source observations, metric definitions, and the benchmark fixture are not measurements.
